name: Census Building Permits Survey (BPS), county-level
measures: New privately-owned housing units authorized by building permits — count and valuation, a leading indicator of future housing supply.
granularity: county and permit-issuing-place (since a 2022 methodology change made county estimates complete rather than sample-based)
update_frequency: monthly (preliminary ~12th workday, revised with county detail ~17th–18th workday)
history_available: monthly county series available for many years; completeness only guaranteed since the Jan 2022 cutoff-sample change
cost: Free, no account needed for the file downloads.
license: US government public data, no restriction found.
relevant_gap: All existing growth signals (rezonings, housing_database, subway_access, planned_catalysts in development.py/transit.py) are either demand-side or policy/infrastructure signals. BPS would be the one direct supply-side signal: more permits filed now can mean more competing inventory 2–3 years out, which cuts the other way from most of today's 'growth' metrics (which treat more development as unambiguously positive).
existing_overlap: Read backend/app/sources/development.py directly: HousingDatabase already pulls NYC DCP's Housing Database (Socrata kyz5-72x5), itself built from DOB job filings, and writes a `pipeline_units_pct` metric from filed+approved+permitted units per NTA, plus `new_units_5y_pct` completions. That's the same underlying concept BPS measures (permits authorizing new housing units) — real overlap, not speculative. The difference is scope: HousingDatabase is NYC-only, while BPS is the one candidate in this batch that would actually serve this project's stated goal of generalizing to any US neighborhood, where no DCP-equivalent exists.
recommendation: Do not recommend for NYC itself — confirmed real overlap with the existing HousingDatabase source's pipeline_units_pct/new_units_5y_pct metrics, so adding BPS there would be redundant. The only scenario where it earns its keep is the national-generalization goal, and even there the access path is a blocker: I could not confirm a documented county-level REST API (Census's api.census.gov/data/timeseries/eits catalog covers national indicators like bfs/m3/ftd, but no 'bps' entry surfaced there; county BPS data appears to live in the separate census.gov/construction/bps bulk file system, meaning fixed-width/CSV text parsing instead of a clean API). Revisit specifically for non-NYC regions once the area-model migration (noted in backend/CLAUDE.md) is further along, not as a near-term NYC addition.
